pass_a_gloss: Tome 1. [Lemma, Isaiah 25:1:] Lord my God, I will glorify you, and I will hymn your name, because you made wonderful things, a counsel ancient, true; may it be, Lord. In the finished book a long discourse came to the prophet, and going through hidden thoughts, about both the devil's perversity and the punishment and penalty that will be upon him, and besides also the overturning of the wicked and opposing powers. And he was adding to these also the proclamation of the kingdom of Christ. For he said that the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem, and before the elders will be glorified. For the sake of all these things, then, the prophet becomes full of great joy, and honours the accomplisher of things so marvellous with praises. For this reason he says: Lord my God, I will glorify you, and I will hymn your name, a counsel ancient and true, and you have done marvellous things. And since about things not yet having happened at that time he says the 'You made', he hints that it has not yet happened, but that it will be in every way and wholly, adding the 'May it be, Lord'. For with the eyes of the mind they were beholding the time of the sojourn as present, but they were in no way ignorant that it was not yet present; and as an ancient counsel, and wonderful things, he calls the mystery of the becoming man of the Only-Begotten, and the things achieved from it for those throughout all the earth. For we have been saved in Christ, foreknown before foundation of world, and made manifest at the last times of the age, as the most wise Paul says. For not new, or lately appearing, is the mystery of Christ, but it had been foreordained before the foundation of the world, and has been made manifest in its own times. [Lemma, Isaiah 25:2:] Because you set cities into a heap, strong cities, for their foundations to fall; and of the ungodly a city will not be built forever. Of the true counsel this too, and of the blameless considerations of the God who prevails in all things, that strong cities be shaken down, and become into a heap, and be as it were levered up from their foundations, and come to be outside hope, from which they will not be able ever to recover. For it will not, he says, be built forever. pass_b_english: “O Lord my God, I will glorify you; I will sing hymns to your name, for you have done wonderful things, an ancient and true counsel. So be it, O Lord” (Isaiah 25:1).

In the book just completed, the prophet spoke at length, and through hidden meanings, about the devil’s perversity, the punishment and judgment that will come upon him, and also the overthrow of the wicked and hostile powers. To these he added the proclamation of Christ’s kingdom. For he said that the Lord will reign in Zion and in Jerusalem, and will be glorified before the elders (Isaiah 24:23). For all these reasons, then, the prophet is filled with great joy and honors with praises the one who accomplished things so marvelous. That is why he says: “O Lord my God, I will glorify you and sing hymns to your name, an ancient and true counsel, and you have done marvelous things.”

Since he says “you have done” about things that had not yet happened at that time, he indicates by adding “So be it, O Lord” that, though it has not yet happened, it will surely happen in every way. For with the eyes of the mind they gazed on the time of his coming as though it were present, yet they were by no means unaware that it was not yet present. He calls the mystery of the Only-Begotten’s becoming man an ancient counsel, and calls what it has accomplished for those throughout all the earth marvelous things.

For we have been saved in Christ, who was foreknown before the foundation of the world but made manifest in the last times of the age (compare 1 Peter 1:20). As the most wise Paul says, the mystery of Christ is not new or lately come to light; it was foreordained before the foundation of the world, but has been made manifest in its own times (compare Titus 1:3).

“For you have made cities a heap, strong cities, so that their foundations might fall; the city of the ungodly will never be built, forever” (Isaiah 25:2). This too belongs to the true counsel and the blameless purposes of God, who is able to do all things: that strong cities should be shaken down and become a heap, be as it were heaved up from their foundations, and be past hope, so that they will never be able to recover. For it will never, he says, be built, forever.

choices.why: The printed ὑπνήσω is a misprint for ὑμνήσω (Isaiah 25:1 Septuagint), as Cyril's own repetition of the lemma shows.
Cyril explains the wish as marking that what 'you have done' had not yet happened.
ἐνανθρώπησις is the Incarnation; the plain English phrase is used.
The words attributed to Paul paraphrase 1 Peter 1:20 and Titus 1:3; both are marked 'compare'.
rejected: citing them as direct Pauline quotations

choices.why: ἀνασφάλλω, to rise again after a fall.
